title: Memphis dry rub
summary: A paprika-forward rib rub with garlic, onion, mustard and a little heat, for ribs served 'dry' with no sauce.

ingredients.note: half sweet, half smoked if you have both

steps: Mix everything together, breaking up lumps with a fork. Store airtight away from light for up to 3 months.
Pat ribs dry, remove the membrane from the bone side and coat with the rub, about 1 tbsp per 225 g of meat (roughly half a rack of baby backs). Refrigerate 1–12 hours if you have time.

Smoke at 110–125 °C (225–260 °F) for 4–5 hours for baby backs or 5–6 for spareribs, until the meat has pulled back from the bones and a rack bends easily when lifted. In an oven, bake on a rack at 135 °C (275 °F), covered with foil for the first two-thirds of the time.
Dust with a little more rub just before serving.
tips: Erythritol does not caramelise like brown sugar; the bark will be less sticky, which suits the 'dry' style.
For 'wet' ribs, brush with Kansas City barbecue sauce in the last 15 minutes.

origin.history: Memphis is famous for pork ribs, served either 'wet' with sauce or 'dry' with only a spice rub. The dry style is often credited to Charlie Vergos's Rendezvous restaurant, which opened in 1948 and dusted its charcoal-grilled ribs with a paprika-heavy seasoning. The city's barbecue identity was later reinforced by its annual barbecue cooking contest, held since the late 1970s.
